summary: @servicetitan/titan-chat-ui preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes an obfuscated 728KB payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs (itself hex-name-obfuscated) downloads the Bun runtime from the oven-sh/bun v1.3.13 GitHub release into a temp directory, chmods it executable, and uses it to execFileSync a sibling file math_init.js under Bun rather than Node. math_init.js is a 727,680-byte single-line '@bun-cjs' bundle at the tarball root, not referenced by main/exports and not present in src/, using obfuscator.io-style hex identifiers (_0xNNNN), a shuffled string-array with a rotator function, and a custom base64-like alphabet decoder to hide its literal strings (URLs, commands, secrets). A React chat UI package has no legitimate need for a second language runtime or an opaque Bun-only bundle executed at install time. The combination — install-time fetch of an alternate language runtime specifically to execute an undeclared obfuscated sibling bundle that Node-based scanners will not evaluate — is the alternate-runtime dropper pattern and causes arbitrary attacker-controlled code execution on every installer's host on npm install.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
